newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela tax law stalls billion dollar oil deals.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela tax law stalls billion dollar oil deals.

text.p: Billion-dollar oil and mining investments in Venezuela are being held up by the stalled passage of key tax legislation, oil industry sources said.
"The oil companies have done seismic surveys and spent a few million here and there," said one lawyer for a major U.S. oil company operating in Venezuela who asked not to be identified.
"But the billion-dollar investments, the big bucks expected from the oil opening, are waiting until the regulations are passed," he said.
Venezuela opened its oil sector for the first time in 20 years in January in a much heralded round of auctions expected to bring in some $10 billion over ten years.
The law exempts companies from paying a 16.5 percent tax on the start-up costs of capital intensive projects.
Although approved by congress in July, "the mechanism that would implement it has not yet been worked out ... everyone is hanging back, delaying investments, until it is," said the source.
Officials at state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA) and the Ministry of Energy and Mines were not immediately available for comment.

"A sense of complacency seems to have set in ... the administration and PdVSA seem to have forgotten ... certain modifications in Venezuela's tax laws," said financial business magazine VenEconomy in an editorial.
"There is a real danger that the Big PetroBucks will not flow into Venezuela as quickly as the administration and PdVSA anticipate."

In addition to the oil opening, Atlantic Richfield Co signed a $3.5 billion deal with PdVSA affiliate Corpoven in August to exploit Venezuela's huge reserves of heavy crude in the Orinocco Tar Belt. Mobil signed a similar $2.3 billion deal with affiliate Lagoven in September.
Venezuela is due to announce details on 20 marginal oil fields as part of its third round of auctioning operating concessions before the end of the week.
